text: Counsel’s brief supporting a motion to dismiss cited several non-existent authorities and misstated the law. He did not dispute this and explained that the miscitations came from using the LexisNexis AI research platform Protégé. LexisNexis then provided the court a letter refuting that he held any subscription to Lexis+ AI or Protégé, so the court recorded concern both about the hallucinated authority and about the attorney’s misrepresentation of where his research came from.
ai_system_name: Protégé / Lexis+ AI (named by counsel; vendor denied he had access)
deployer: Tyrone A. Blackburn (T.A. Blackburn Law, PLLC), defence counsel and himself a named defendant
canonical_source_conflicted: Non-existent judicial authority and misstatements of law in briefing on a Rule 12(b)(6) motion
mitigation_gap: Counsel filed AI-derived research without verification and then attributed it to a product he did not have, so the account of the failure was itself unreliable.
reliance_or_harm: Public admonition recorded in a published opinion and order, expressly intended to deter future misconduct, with a warning that further misconduct may lead to sanctions or a disciplinary referral; the court declined to strike the submissions or award fees.
